cavagna_heglund_taylor_1977.cite: Cavagna GA, Heglund NC, Taylor CR (1977). Mechanical work in terrestrial locomotion: two basic mechanisms for minimizing energy expenditure. Am J Physiol 233(5):R243-261.
cavagna_heglund_taylor_1977.verified_via: NCBI esearch/esummary/efetch (full abstract text), live, this session.
cavagna_heglund_taylor_1977.key_numbers_quoted_verbatim: "Walking, in all animals (as in man), involves an alternate transfer between gravitational-potential energy and kinetic energy within each stride (as takes place in a pendulum). This transfer is greatest at intermediate walking speeds and can account for up to 70% of the total energy changes taking place within a stride, leaving only 30% to be supplied by muscles. No kinetic-gravitational energy transfer takes place during running, hopping, and trotting, but energy is conserved by another mechanism: an elastic 'bounce' of the body."
cavagna_heglund_taylor_1977.role: primary external anchor for Part 1 / Part 4 (energy recovery magnitude + the run-side null/contrast).

carr_mcgee_2009.cite: Carr CE, McGee J (2009). The Apollo Number: space suits, self-support, and the walk-run transition. PLoS ONE 4(8):e6614.
carr_mcgee_2009.verified_via: NCBI esearch/esummary/efetch (full abstract text), live, this session.
carr_mcgee_2009.key_numbers_quoted_verbatim: "The walk-run transition (denoted *) correlates with the Froude Number (Fr = v(2)/gL, velocity v, gravitational acceleration g, leg length L). Human unsuited Fr* is relatively constant (approximately 0.5) with gravity but increases substantially with decreasing gravity below approximately 0.4 g, rising to 0.9 in 1/6 g."
carr_mcgee_2009.role: primary numeric anchor for Part 3 (Fr~0.5 human walk-run transition) -- the exact number is directly quoted from this abstract, not from the older Alexander citation below.

diedrich_warren_1995.cite: Diedrich FJ, Warren WH Jr (1995). Why change gaits? Dynamics of the walk-run transition. J Exp Psychol Hum Percept Perform 21(1):183-202.
diedrich_warren_1995.verified_via: NCBI esearch/esummary/efetch (full abstract text), live, this session.
diedrich_warren_1995.key_numbers: Treadmill experiments (Exp 1: varied speed; Exp 2: dissociated speed/frequency/stride-length): "The transition occurred at the equal-energy separatrix between gaits... Results are consistent with a dynamic theory of locomotion in which preferred gaits are characterized by stable phase relationships and minimum energy expenditure." Independent behavioral confirmation that the human walk-run transition is a real, sharp, dynamically-determined phenomenon (complementary to the Froude-number parametrization in Carr & McGee 2009), not a numeric source for the 0.5 figure itself.
diedrich_warren_1995.role: secondary/complementary anchor for Part 3 (confirms the transition phenomenon independently of the Froude formalism).

vaughan_omalley_2005.cite: Vaughan CL, O'Malley MJ (2005). Froude and the contribution of naval architecture to our understanding of bipedal locomotion. Gait Posture 21(3):350-362.
vaughan_omalley_2005.verified_via: NCBI esearch/esummary/efetch (full abstract text), live, this session.
vaughan_omalley_2005.key_numbers_quoted_verbatim: "The Froude number, defined as Fr = v2/gL, where v is velocity, g is gravitational acceleration and L is a characteristic linear dimension (such as leg length), has found widespread application in the biomechanics of bipedal locomotion."
vaughan_omalley_2005.role: confirms the Fr=v^2/gL formalism itself as the standard dynamic-similarity criterion for bipedal gait; cites Alexander's popularization of it. Does not itself give the numeric 0.5 transition value in its abstract.

alexander_1989.cite: Alexander RM (1989). Optimization and gaits in the locomotion of vertebrates. Physiol Rev 69(4):1199-1227.
alexander_1989.verified_via: NCBI esearch/esummary/efetch, live, this session -- title/journal/date/DOI/PMID all confirmed live. efetch returned NO abstract text for this record (MEDLINE has none on file for this older review).
alexander_1989.key_numbers: NOT independently extracted this session (no abstract text available). Cited for historical/intellectual lineage only (Vaughan & O'Malley 2005 credits Alexander with popularizing Fr for animal locomotion) -- the numeric ~0.5 claim in this doc is anchored instead to Carr & McGee 2009's directly-quoted abstract text, not to this citation.
alexander_1989.role: disclosed as a verified-but-textually-unconfirmed lineage citation, not a load-bearing numeric source -- an honest gap, not hidden.

oberg_karsznia_oberg_1993.cite: Oberg T, Karsznia A, Oberg K (1993). Basic gait parameters: reference data for normal subjects, 10-79 years of age. J Rehabil Res Dev 30(2):210-223.
oberg_karsznia_oberg_1993.verified_via: NCBI esearch/esummary/efetch (full abstract text), live, this session.
oberg_karsznia_oberg_1993.key_numbers: 233 healthy subjects (116 men, 117 women), 10-79 years, 5.5m walkway; "results are presented in a series of reference tables for slow, normal, and fast gait" with mean/SD/CI/prediction intervals. Confirms the EXISTENCE of a speed-stratified normative gait-timing framework; the abstract itself does not hand over the double-support-time table values, so this doc's explanation of why measured DS%=33.8% exceeds the commonly-quoted ~20% (this trial's slower 1.06 m/s speed) is a directionally-argued, not table-verified, honest gap.
oberg_karsznia_oberg_1993.role: context/existence-anchor for Part 2's double-support-vs-speed discussion; not a precise numeric anchor this session.

overall_verdict: 7/7 pre-registered gates PASS on the twin's own measured subject2_walking1 trial. The inverted-pendulum energy-exchange model is confirmed directly (not just via literature): KE and PE trade out of phase (r consistently and strongly negative, 4/4 real-data combinations), recovery magnitude is substantial and Cavagna-consistent (52-80% real-data range; 60-69% on the more classically-correct full-stride reconstruction), the GRF shows the canonical double-hump M-shape, double-support occupies a walking-consistent (not running, not degenerate) 33.8% of the cycle, and the Froude number (0.108) sits 4.6x below the empirically-established human walk-run transition (~0.5). An OODA-forced diagnostic explained (rather than hid) the initial half-step recovery spread via the DS1-collision/DS2-push-off mechanistic distinction, and a specificity check (reversed-proxy splice) confirmed the full-stride reconstruction is not manufacturing a signal from arbitrary input.
symmetric_qc_open_items: Single trial, single (partially reconstructed) stride -- no repeated-stride ensemble exists in this data to separate genuine cycle-to-cycle variability from this method's own measurement noise.

The full-stride reconstruction mirrors a measured quarter-phase to complete the (data-truncated) missing quarter -- a disclosed, symmetry-justified approximation, not raw data; the reversed-proxy specificity check shows real sensitivity to getting this construction's temporal direction right.

Measured double-support fraction (33.8%) exceeds the commonly-quoted '~20%' figure; explained via this trial's slower-than-typical 1.06 m/s speed and the established (but not table-verified this session) inverse speed/double-support relationship -- Oberg et al. 1993's abstract confirms such normative tables exist but does not hand over the exact slope.

Alexander 1989 (PMID 2678167) is a verified-real but textually-unconfirmed (no MEDLINE abstract) citation for historical lineage only; the numeric Fr~0.5 claim is anchored to Carr & McGee 2009's directly-quoted abstract instead, not to Alexander.
2D sagittal-plane simplification (mediolateral GRF and internal/rotational KE excluded) matches Cavagna's own classic method but is a real simplification, disclosed not hidden.

Two independent mass estimates (78.2 kg established vs. 79.24 kg static-trial-derived) differ by 1.33%, not reconciled to sub-percent precision this session -- both carried through the analysis in parallel rather than one discarded.

The dysfunction/pathology mapping (antalgic, Trendelenburg, spastic, Parkinsonian festination) is explicitly conceptual this session -- no pathological-gait trial exists in this repo's read-accessible data to test it against; flagged as proposed_cell, not claimed as measured.
